one_liner: Writes the code behind apps and websites people use every day.
job_roles: Frontend Developer | Backend Developer | Full-Stack Developer | Android Developer | iOS Developer | Software Engineer | API Developer | Smart Contract Engineer
industrial_sectors: IT-ITES | BFSI | RASCI | TSSC | HSSC | MESC | LSC
entrance_exams: JEE Main (B.Tech) | CUET (BCA/B.Sc) | BITSAT | VITEEE | SRMJEEE | COMEDK
self_emp_route: Freelance and contract development, or founding a product company.
ai_reason: Syntax and boilerplate are skill, and that is what AI now does. What remains is deciding what to build, how it should behave at the edges, and why the last approach failed. Junior implementation work shrinks; deciding what is worth implementing does not.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. Maths helps but BCA and B.Sc IT accept most streams. -> degree: B.Tech CSE, BCA or B.Sc Computer Science (3-4 years) -> portfolio: Working projects on GitHub — this is what actually gets you hired
nuances: [job_roles] Smart Contract Engineer is retained here after Blockchain was dropped as a standalone profession. The Indian Web3 market is too thin to support a separate career, but the role exists inside general development.

one_liner: Builds and looks after websites and online shops for small businesses, usually freelance.
job_roles: WordPress Developer | Shopify Developer | Webflow Developer | Website Maintenance Freelancer | E-commerce Store Setup Specialist
self_emp_route: Freelance from the first client, then a small agency. This is the most common self-employment in Sector 1 and also the most exposed to no-code tools taking the low end.
ai_reason: Almost pure execution skill on digital output, which is the most exposed combination in the sector. What survives is the client relationship — knowing a local business well enough to run their store. Building the pages themselves is already largely automated. Raised clarity 20->25. The durable part of this work is understanding what a local business actually needs versus what they asked for — that is 'for whom' clarity. Page-building itself is fully exposed.
path_to_entry: self_study: Learn WordPress or Shopify — free, online, no gatekeeper -> portfolio: Build 3-5 real sites, even unpaid, for local businesses -> first_clients: Freelance platforms or local word of mouth
review_reason: SELF-EMPLOYMENT CEILING OWED. Employed mid-career is 4.5 lakh and people in this profession routinely go independent, but no reliable Indian figure was found for what they earn once they do. Until it exists the record understates the profession, which is exactly the defect this field was added to fix. The route is recorded; the number is not.
nuances: [demand_signal] Demand is declining. Wix, Shopify and no-code builders have absorbed most of the simple brochure-and-catalogue work that defined this job, and generative tools are taking the rest of the low end. What survives is integration, performance and commerce operations for businesses that have outgrown a template. Still listed - Indian small business is enormous and the work has not vanished - but the direction is down.

one_liner: Builds video games and 3D interactive worlds — the code, the rules and the environments.
job_roles: Game Programmer | Unity Developer | Unreal Engine Developer | Game Designer | Level Designer | Mobile Game Developer | AR Developer | VR Developer | Simulation Developer
self_emp_route: Indie studio or contract development for larger studios.
ai_reason: Asset production and boilerplate gameplay code are exposed. Judging what is actually fun, and why a level feels wrong, is clarity that does not transfer to a model.
role_spread: [Game Designer, Level Designer] higher: openness, existential, verbal / lower: logical, attention_span
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream -> training: Game development diploma, or self-taught Unity/Unreal -> portfolio: 2-3 finished playable games or XR demos. Studios hire on this, not marks.
nuances: [job_roles] AR and VR development is merged in here rather than standing alone. The engines are the same - Unity and Unreal - the studios are largely the same, and India's standalone XR market is small. Confirmed as a merge rather than a separate profession.

one_liner: Teaches computers to recognise patterns, predict things and answer in language.
job_roles: Machine Learning Engineer | Data Scientist | Natural Language Processing Engineer | Computer Vision Engineer | MLOps Engineer | Applied AI Engineer | LLM Application Engineer
industrial_sectors: IT-ITES | BFSI | HSSC | RASCI | ASCI | LSC | TSSC
entrance_exams: JEE Main (B.Tech) | CUET (BCA/B.Sc) | BITSAT | VITEEE | COMEDK
self_emp_route: Independent consulting or founding a product company, on the strength of a portfolio.
ai_reason: Model training is increasingly automated. Framing the problem, judging whether the data answers the question, and deciding when the model is good enough to ship are not.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream, but Maths makes this far easier -> degree: B.Tech, BCA, B.Sc CS/Statistics/Maths (3-4 years) -> specialisation: Strong linear algebra and probability, plus real ML projects
nuances: [economics] The early band reflects a hiring market that has moved fast in both directions. Treat the ceiling as cycle-dependent rather than structural. || [degree_dependency] Tagged undergrad because that is what the hiring market overwhelmingly screens on, not because the knowledge is unreachable otherwise. This is the profession in Sector 1 where a demonstrated portfolio - published models, competition results, real deployed systems - most often overrides the absence of a matching degree. The tag is the destination and the usual door; it is not the only door. || [economics] The widest band in the taxonomy, and the width is real rather than an artefact. The same job title covers someone fine-tuning an existing model against a vendor API and someone training models at scale in a research-adjacent team, and Indian pay for the second is set by a small global market while pay for the first is set by ordinary IT services rates.

one_liner: Turns messy company data into charts and answers that help people decide.
job_roles: Business Data Analyst | Business Intelligence Developer | Product Analyst | Reporting Analyst | Power BI / Tableau Developer | Marketing Analytics Executive
industrial_sectors: IT-ITES | BFSI | RASCI | LSC | HSSC | TSSC | MEPSC
self_emp_route: Freelance analytics and dashboard work for small businesses.
ai_reason: Reporting and dashboard-building is skill on digital output — squarely in the blast radius. Product Analyst survives because it depends on knowing which question is worth asking and arguing for a decision.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream -> training: Analytics certification — Excel, SQL, Power BI or Tableau -> portfolio: 3-4 dashboards built on real public datasets
nuances: [degree_dependency] Tagged certificate because the certification-plus-portfolio route genuinely works in India. Many employers still screen on a degree, so the route is real but not frictionless.

one_liner: Builds the pipes and storage that carry a company's data safely from place to place.
job_roles: Data Engineer | Database Administrator | ETL Developer | Data Warehouse Engineer | Big Data Engineer | Analytics Engineer
industrial_sectors: IT-ITES | BFSI | TSSC | RASCI | LSC | PSSC
entrance_exams: JEE Main (B.Tech) | CUET (BCA/B.Sc) | BITSAT | VITEEE | COMEDK
ai_reason: Pipeline boilerplate is generated well by AI. Judging correctness, cost and what to do when data is wrong at 3am is clarity with real consequences.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream -> degree: B.Tech, BCA or B.Sc Computer Science -> specialisation: SQL, Python, and a cloud data stack

one_liner: Defends computer systems from attack, and tests them by trying to break in first.
job_roles: Security Operations Centre (SOC) Analyst | Penetration Tester | Application Security Engineer | Cloud Security Engineer | Digital Forensics Analyst | Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) Analyst | Incident Response Analyst
industrial_sectors: IT-ITES | BFSI | TSSC | PSSC | HYSSC | SMSSC | HSSC
self_emp_route: Independent penetration testing and audit practice, always under written scope.
ai_reason: L1 alert triage is skill and heavily exposed. Adversarial judgement — attackers adapt, so the right response is never a fixed procedure — is clarity, as is being the accountable human during a breach.
role_spread: [Penetration Tester] higher: openness, reasoning, confidence / lower: agreeableness, dogmatism
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream -> certification: CompTIA Security+, CEH, or OSCP for the offensive side -> practice: Capture-the-flag competitions and home lab work
nuances: [degree_dependency] Tagged certificate rather than undergrad on the strength of how hiring actually works: OSCP, CEH, CISSP and equivalent certifications are what employers screen on, and the field takes entrants from IT support and networking backgrounds without a security degree. A computer science degree helps and is the common path; it is not the gate. || [job_roles] Penetration Tester and Red Team Analyst are offensive-security roles, and the skills are the same ones an attacker uses. What separates the profession from the crime is authorisation - a signed scope agreement before any testing - and that distinction belongs in front of a school-age student at the point the role is shown, not after.

one_liner: Keeps apps running on the internet — fast, always on, and cheap to run.
job_roles: Cloud Engineer (AWS / Azure / GCP) | DevOps Engineer | Site Reliability Engineer | Platform Engineer | Systems Administrator | Kubernetes Engineer
self_emp_route: Independent cloud consulting, usually after certifications and production experience.
ai_reason: Config and scripting is exposed. Deciding architecture trade-offs, and being answerable when production is down, is not.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream -> certification: AWS, Azure or Google Cloud associate certification -> practice: Deploy and run your own projects end to end

one_liner: Hunts for bugs and broken behaviour before customers ever see them.
job_roles: Manual QA Tester | Automation Test Engineer | Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET) | Performance Test Engineer | Mobile App Tester | Accessibility Tester
ai_reason: Manual QA is the highest skill-to-clarity ratio in the sector: repetitive execution on digital output. SDET and performance testing carry more clarity and are materially safer. Anyone entering should target automation from day one.
role_spread: [Manual QA Tester, Accessibility Tester] higher: attention_span, conscientiousness / lower: logical, openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream -> training: Software testing certification (ISTQB is the common one) -> specialisation: Move to automation early — Selenium or Playwright
nuances: [ai_exposure] The high band is driven by MANUAL QA. SDET and performance testing sit in a materially different position. Anyone entering should target automation from day one rather than manual testing.

one_liner: Fixes the computers, wifi and networks an office runs on.
job_roles: IT Helpdesk Technician | Desktop Support Engineer | Network Engineer | Network Operations Centre (NOC) Engineer | Field Service Technician (IT) | Hardware & Networking Technician
industrial_sectors: IT-ITES | TSSC | ESSCI | BFSI | RASCI | HSSC
self_emp_route: Own AMC business maintaining IT for small offices and shops.
ai_reason: Skill-heavy but most of that skill is physical — crimping cable, replacing hardware, walking to a site. L1 phone scripts are exposed; field and network work is not. Raised clarity 20->25. Helpdesk work is the classic gap between what a user reports and what is actually wrong — diagnosing the real problem behind the stated one is 'what' and 'for whom' clarity.
role_spread: [IT Helpdesk Technician, Desktop Support Engineer] higher: extraversion, emotional_intelligence, agreeableness / lower: logical, attention_span
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream -> training: ITI or polytechnic diploma in computer hardware and networking -> certification: CompTIA A+ or Cisco CCNA to move up
nuances: [economics] Listed as a destination, and it is a real one: network, systems and NOC work is a durable career with certification ladders - CCNA onwards - that raise pay without a degree. It is also the cheapest technical entry point in this sector, which is why the low band is not the whole story. A student should know both that it pays least at entry and that it is one of the few routes into cloud and infrastructure work that does not require an engineering seat.

one_liner: Writes the code that lives inside machines — cars, meters, drones, smart devices.
job_roles: Embedded Software Engineer | Firmware Developer | IoT Application Developer | RTOS Engineer | Automotive Software Engineer | Device Driver Developer
industrial_sectors: ESSCI | ASDC | IT-ITES | AASSC | PSSC | IASC | SMSSC
entrance_exams: JEE Main Paper 1 | JEE Advanced | BITSAT | VITEEE | SRMJEEE | COMEDK
ai_reason: Protected on two layers at once: deep foundational knowledge of how hardware actually behaves, plus physical bench work. Debugging a board with an oscilloscope is not a text problem.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics and Maths compulsory, plus one of Chemistry/Biology/Vocational -> entrance_exam: JEE Main Paper 1, or a state or private engineering entrance -> degree: B.Tech in Electronics, ECE or Electrical (4 years) -> specialisation: Embedded C, microcontrollers, hands-on board work
entry_window: route limit: JEE Main — admits only recent class 12 passouts | bypass: 3-year engineering diploma, then lateral entry into B.Tech year 2 (generally no upper age limit); B.Sc graduate lateral entry into B.Tech year 2; Private university admission
nuances: [entry_window] The lateral-entry bypass is reliable at national level. AICTE norms set NO maximum age for diploma-to-B.Tech lateral entry, so the three-year JEE window constrains one route and not the profession. What varies is the state: some state LEET rules and some institutions apply an 18 to 26 band, and the diploma aggregate requirement runs 45 to 50 percent. A student should check their own state's LEET, but no state closes the door outright.

one_liner: Sets up and customises the big software that large companies run on.
job_roles: SAP Consultant (FICO / MM / ABAP) | Salesforce Developer | Salesforce Administrator | ERP Functional Consultant | ServiceNow Developer | Oracle Applications Consultant | Microsoft Power Platform Developer | RPA Developer
industrial_sectors: IT-ITES | BFSI | RASCI | SMSSC | LSC | CGSC | MEPSC
self_emp_route: Independent implementation consulting, usually after certification and client relationships.
ai_reason: Platform configuration is exposed. Sitting with a client's finance team to work out why their process is the way it is, and owning a migration that could halt their business, is clarity. Raised clarity 40->45. The job is understanding why a client's finance or supply process is the way it is before changing it. Strongly 'for whom' — configuration is the exposed part.
role_spread: [ERP Functional Consultant, Salesforce Administrator] higher: verbal, extraversion, emotional_intelligence / lower: logical
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. Commerce is genuinely useful for the finance modules. -> degree: Any bachelor's — B.Com and BBA are common routes, not just B.Tech -> certification: SAP, Salesforce or ServiceNow platform certification
nuances: [job_roles] RPA and no-code automation are merged in here as enterprise tooling rather than kept as a separate career. The work is configuring a vendor platform against a client's process, which is this profession's skill set applied to a different tool. Confirmed as a merge.

one_liner: Sits between users and coders, and turns 'what we need' into 'what to build'.
job_roles: IT Business Analyst | Systems Analyst | Functional Consultant | Requirements Analyst | Technical Business Analyst (BFSI)
industrial_sectors: IT-ITES | BFSI | HSSC | RASCI | TSSC | MEPSC
ai_reason: Now the safest desk job in the sector. Drafting is exposed, but 55% of the work is getting people who disagree to state what they actually want — that is clarity and it does not erode.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream -> degree: Any bachelor's — BBA, B.Com, BCA and B.Tech all work -> skills: SQL, requirement documentation, and a domain (banking, retail, health)
nuances: [professional_sector] Sits in Software & Computing rather than Business because in Indian IT services this is a technical job family — SQL, systems, requirements. The craft is closer to computing than to management.

one_liner: Builds the software tools and pipelines that film and animation studios use to make effects.
job_roles: VFX Pipeline Developer | Technical Artist | Tools Developer (Maya / Houdini / Nuke) | Rendering Engineer | CAD & Simulation Software Developer
self_emp_route: Freelance for studios, or a small pipeline and tools shop.
ai_reason: Revised down from high. Generative models hit execution skill hard, but pipeline and tools work is increasingly about design judgement — knowing what artists need and what a shot should look like — rather than hand-crafting output. The skill layer erodes; the design clarity does not.
role_spread: [Technical Artist] higher: spatial, openness, musical / lower: attention_span
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream, but Maths is close to essential here -> degree: B.Tech CSE, B.Sc CS, or a VFX/animation diploma for the pipeline track -> portfolio: Python tools for Maya or Houdini, or rendering demos with source code
